text:
cory: Heads-up — provisioning backlog in us-east1. Multiple GPU attach failures; provisioner logs show "attach failed: scratch iops exceeded" across a cohort. Seeing sustained NVMe IOPS ~850k on ~300 nodes, expected ~200k.

maria: Link to the dashboard?

cory: https://grafana.redwood/d/ops/ephemeral-iops?orgId=1&refresh=30s — spike lines up with the janitor rollout at 1768009000.

jamal: Are we sure it’s janitor? Could be a deep-scrub or a background snapshot job. Any fstrim backlog?

cory: stack traces + janitor-controller events both show heavy scrub starts. Janitor concurrency jumped to 6 after the rollout.

sre-oncall: Sharing iostat from a hit node (nvme hot):
```
Device:        r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1      1200  33000   4800  125000   3.21  0.05  99.8
```

janitor-bot: Janitor: starting group scrub_A on node set us-east1-cohort with concurrency=6 (run id=jan-7842).

maria: Can we throttle janitor concurrency immediately and roll back the change? Also consider disabling deep-scrub window for next 2 hours.

jamal: I just rolled a rollback to reduce janitor concurrency to 2 for us-east1 via canary patch `rollout/7842 -> concurrency=2` (pushed at 1768010005).

cory: Provisioner logs post-patch: attach_fail_rate 18% -> 3% in last 5m. Latency tail improved. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: Created incident INC-2026-2234 and added a 1-hour watch. Placed non-prod GPU requests to fallback region us-west2 for the next 30m to reduce pressure.

maria: Agree with fallback for non-prod. For prod, we should add an IOPS-aware attach gate so janitor backs off when attach latency > 200ms. Cost tradeoff note: fallback increases cross-region egress for some workloads.

jamal: Quick config we applied to the janitor to prevent recurrence: reduced concurrency to 2, added a soft rate-limit (50 iops per node for scrub workers), and added exponential backoff on scrub retries. Will push an infra PR for defaulting to those limits.

cory: Action items: 1) Keep janitor concurrency at 2 for 2 hours and monitor iops + attach_fail_rate. 2) Temporarily disable scheduled deep-scrubs overnight for us-east1. 3) Short-term routing: non-prod -> us-west2. 4) Longer-term: implement IOPS-aware attach gating and model prefix caching to reduce hot-read pressure.

maria: Filing ticket OPTIMIZE-451 to audit hot-model prefix cache and a follow-up infra RFC for attach gating.

sre-oncall: I’ll keep the incident open and post updates every 15m. If attach_fail_rate goes above 10% again we’ll escalate to SEV.

cory: Thanks everyone. Still watching logs — will post a final status in 30m.

maria: Thanks — great quick rollback. :heart:
